text:
maria_gonzalez: Hey, escalating a customer issue — Go client started failing auth after we asked them to upgrade to our latest SDK. They say requests return 401 from the hosted API. Error log attached.

kevin_hu: Can you paste the error and their go.mod + how they installed the client?

maria_gonzalez: Error: `redwood: unauthorized (invalid token)` in response body, HTTP 401.
Log snippet:
```
2024/04/02 09:12:05 request failed: status=401 body={"error":"redwood: unauthorized (invalid token)"}
```
They upgraded by running `go get github.com/redwood-inc/inference-go@latest` then `go mod tidy`. go.mod has: 
```
module customer/app
\ngo 1.20
\nrequire (
    github.com/redwood-inc/inference-go v0.0.0-20240301abcdef // indirect
)
\nreplace github.com/redwood-inc/inference-go => github.com/redwood-inc/inference-go v0.0.0-20240301abcdef
```

maria_gonzalez: They also have a local replace in their monorepo pointing to `../internal/inference-go` so the tag behavior is weird.

support_bot: Ticket #INC-2491 created and linked to this thread.

kevin_hu: Two immediate suspects: 1) The binary they're pulling via replace isn't built with our auth change (we rolled token header rename in v1.4.0). 2) They might have a caching proxy serving an older commit.

kevin_hu: Quick repro steps for them:
1) run `go clean -modcache`
2) remove the local `replace` directive or point it at a tagged release 
3) `go get github.com/redwood-inc/inference-go@v1.4.0`
4) `go mod tidy`
5) rebuild and retry request

sanjay_patel: Also verify `go list -m -json github.com/redwood-inc/inference-go` to confirm the resolved version and `replace` is not overriding it. If they see a pseudo-version like `v0.0.0-20240301abcdef` that's the problem.

maria_gonzalez: I ran the steps with the customer on a shared session. `go list -m -json` returned the local path because of the `replace` — they were still using our older commit which expects `X-Redwood-Token` header (we switched to `Authorization: Bearer <token>` in v1.4.0).

kevin_hu: OK that matches. Short-term workaround: change their code to set `X-Redwood-Token` header, but better is to remove `replace` and use released tag.

maria_gonzalez: Customer can't change their monorepo fairly easily. Can we publish a compatibility tag that accepts both headers? Maybe cut v1.4.1 with a shim that checks both `Authorization` and `X-Redwood-Token` for a short period.

eng_release_lead: @kevin_hu @sanjay_patel we can do a quick patch release. Plan: create v1.4.1 that adds fallback support, run unit tests, publish tag and update release notes. I can cut the tag in ~30m if engineering approves.

sanjay_patel: Patch LGTM. Keep change minimal: in auth.go, add: `token := req.Header.Get("Authorization") if token=="" { token = req.Header.Get("X-Redwood-Token") }` plus one unit test. Backport to main and tag v1.4.1.

kevin_hu: After publish, ask customer to run `go get github.com/redwood-inc/inference-go@v1.4.1` and remove the `replace`. Also recommend `go clean -modcache` then rebuild.

support_bot: Patch release job queued: release/v1.4.1 (CI#4523).

eng_release_lead: Tag v1.4.1 pushed and release artifacts uploaded. Release notes: "compat: Accept legacy X-Redwood-Token header to ease migrations".

maria_gonzalez: Sent the upgrade steps to the customer. They applied `go get github.com/redwood-inc/inference-go@v1.4.1`, removed the `replace`, ran `go mod tidy`, rebuilt and confirmed requests succeed. No more 401s.

kevin_hu: Great. We should add a short doc in devex about common `replace` pitfalls and publish a migration note about header rename.

maria_gonzalez: Filing a docs PR now with example `go list -m -json` output and the exact `go get` steps.

sanjay_patel: Also let's add a debug helper to the SDK that logs resolved module version at startup when `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1`, so we can quickly see if someone is running a pseudo-version or local replace.

eng_release_lead: Noted. I'll queue that as a follow-up in backlog.

maria_gonzalez: Closing the support incident after customer confirmation. Thanks team :tada:
